chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Resurrection except for three pairs of eyes: an eye that wept out of fear of God; an eye that was held back from looking at what God has forbidden; and an eye that stayed awake at night in the cause of God.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three pairs of eyes that will not weep on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the eschatological reward for sensory discipline, categorizing the 'three eyes' as those marked by *khushu'* (awe), *ghadd* (averting from sin), and *sahar* (nightly vigilance in jihad or worship). It underscores the Shia emphasis on the physical body as a site of spiritual struggle, linking the preservation of sight to both inner piety and active devotion in the path of God.
